title: Do StrongReject Scores Predict Real-World Jailbreak Resistance? A Construct Validity Study

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Exceptionally important: if StrongReject scores do not predict adaptive attack resistance, the entire evaluation pipeline needs rethinking. This is a foundational validity question for the field's primary measurement tool.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses AISafetyLab for standardized attacks and StrongReject for scoring. Running adaptive attacks (GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR) requires setup but tools exist. 5-8 models is many to run. Medium difficulty with existing tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 5-8 models, 3 attack types each, plus StrongReject scoring, plus correlation analysis. Running GCG/AutoDAN on 5-8 models is compute-intensive and time-consuming. Exceeds 30 hours unless reduced to 3 models and 2 attacks.
